title: Project SOCIAL (Step Out, Connect In-person, Abandon Likes)
official: Project SOCIAL (Step Out, Connect In-person, Abandon Likes): Targeting Adolescents' Social Media Use and Real-time Conversations to Improve Well-being
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine if reducing social media use or increasing deep conversations improves adolescents' mental health and well-being. The participants will be adolescents in the 10th grade at specified rural West Virginia High Schools. Plan is to recruit approximately 400 students. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does reducing social media to less than 1 hour per day improve adolescents' well-being and reduce symptoms of anxiety and depression?
2. Does having one 10-minute deep conversation per day improve adolescents' well-being and reduce symptoms of anxiety and depression?
3. Does reducing social media use or increasing deep conversations show more improvements to well-being than journaling or no intervention?
4. Why do some adolescents benefit from less social media or more deep conversations? What factors help explain this?
5. Do some adolescents benefit more or less than others from the intervention conditions? Participants will be randomized into one of four groups to see whether reducing social media use or increasing real-time conversations improves mental health.

   1. Social Media Reduction: limit social media use to less than 1 hour per day.
   2. Conversation Increase: have one meaningful 10-minute conversation each day.
   3. Journaling: complete 10 minutes of expressive writing each day.
   4. Control: continue usual activities without changing behavior.

Participants will be expected to:

1. Complete surveys at 4 different timepoints:

   1. baseline before week of baseline daily reports (Session 1),
   2. after the two-week intervention and daily reports (Session 3),
   3. 2-week follow-up after Session 3 (Session 4),
   4. 2-month follow-up after Session 3 (Session 5)
2. Complete brief daily reports during a 1-week baseline period and a 2-week intervention period.
3. Follow the assigned intervention for 2 weeks.

With rates of depression, anxiety, and loneliness increasing among adolescents today, this study will provide much needed evidence on whether reducing social media or increasing real-time deep conversations (in-person or on the phone) significantly improves teens' emotional health. This study will also identify what types of teens are more likely to benefit from these interventions and why. If effective, the project would give novel intervention options to help teens develop healthier social habits and improve their mental health.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adolescents in 10th grade at the schools that are collaborating to collect data;
* Participants must be able to read English and understand spoken English;
* Participants must use social media for one hour or more each day

Exclusion Criteria:

* Adolescents without social media account or that use social media less that one hour a day
* Adolescents that are unable to read or speak English
